transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Alex Rivera (Nimbus ML Eng), Samira Patel (Nimbus Head of Platform), Tom Lee (Nimbus Product)

Summary: quick review of last week's benchmark, discuss model selection and pinning strategy for pilot, define rollback/fallback policy, agree next steps for Dedicated eval and security checks. Transcript quality medium; some auto-transcript noise.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we' re on for 45 minutes today. Quick agenda — benchmark recap, model catalog choices, pinning/rollout plan, fallback/rollback test, and action items. Alex you said you had new numbers?
[00:18] Alex: Yeah thanks Lena. So we ran the Redwood hosted baseline and a dedicated config; the numbers I have here are p50s around 220 ms on the hosted for short prompts, p95 spikes when we hit longer contexts to around 1.2s. Dedicated with 8-bit quant and batching got p50 to about 180 ms but p95 still around 900 ms in heavy tail. There's also throughput tradeoffs when we increase concurrency.
[00:38] Marco: ok that's in line with expectations — looks like KV cache hit rates and prefix caching will help on your repeat queries; I noticed your prefix reuse was roughly 40% which means caching yields benefit. Also we saw tokenization mismatches causing some micro headroom loss, the model variant we ran had a different tokenizer mapping.
[00:58] Samira: question — when you say dedicated with 8-bit quant, are we losing noticeable quality? Our product team is sensitive to hallucinations.
[01:12] Marco: good call. In our eval set quality drop was minimal for the short prompts, a small increase in factual errors for very long context prompts. For your golden set, the ROUGE/EM-ish metrics were within 2-4% for most intents. We can pin to a non-quantized variant for critical flows and use quantized for bulk throughput.
[01:36] Tom: So model pinning — is that at the model identifier level or can we pin by version and fallback to a lower-cost variant?
[01:44] Lena: both. Redwood supports model version pinning and routing policies. You can pin traffic to say rwd-llama2-70b-v1 and have an automatic fallback to rwd-llama2-70b-q4 when latency spikes or capacity issues occur. The catalog comparison we shared yesterday shows compatible fallback families.
[02:08] Alex: We also want to test rollbacks if a new model causes regressions. How fast is rollback?
[02:16] Marco: Rollbacks are near-instant at the routing layer — typically within seconds for new requests. But warm-up and KV cache cold starts will cause some latency blips; we recommend a canary window and a traffic ramp so you can judge quality before full cutover.
[02:36] Priya: I'll add that to the rollout playbook we share. Also, Samira you mentioned compliance — we already have a SOC 2 pack in the security folder, but for Private you'll need KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC peering.
[02:56] Samira: yep, about KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys and rotation? We have a strict rotation schedule.
[03:04] Marco: Yes, we support external KMS/HSM with rotation policies. There was a small doc naming mismatch in the auto-transcript last week where we called it K-M-S but spelled it weird in the doc, we'll send the correct security checklist.
[03:22] Alex: One more data thing — retention. We need to ensure we can disable retention on the pilot data for certain endpoints.
[03:29] Lena: You can configure retention per route; for the pilot we suggest disabled retention + VPC. We'll put that in the configuration template.
[03:38] Tom: From product POV, we care about fallbacks when the model halluc in clinical cases. Can we route critical patient-facing queries to the non-quantized variant always?
[03:50] Marco: Absolutely — that's a routing policy. You can mark routes as "critical" and pin them to higher-quality variants; other background tasks use optimized quantized variants.
[04:02] Alex: On the benchmark details, can you share the CSV with per-sequence latencies and the config used? We want to reproduce it in our infra.
[04:11] Marco: Yep will share the raw results and the exact inference config including kernels, continuous batching params, micro-batching, sequence-length distribution. Expect that by Thursday.
[04:23] Samira: On Dedicated sizing — you mentioned burst capacity. What's the lead time to spin up extra nodes if we need more for a spike?
[04:32] Lena: For Dedicated we allocate reserved pools; we can preconfigure autoscale policies with burst capacity to absorb occasional spikes. If you need new reserved cards we typically see a provisioning window of a few days depending on region, but bursts can be configured for minutes to hours depending on pool headroom.
[04:51] Tom: Any competitor notes we should be aware of? We did a quick bench against Anthropic and OpenAI last week and saw similar latency but pricing differences.
[05:00] Lana — oops sorry — Lena: yeah competitors differ in their tokenization and cost model; Redwood's differentiation is routing policies, deterministic rollouts, and the caching in the serving runtime.
[05:12] Alex: On pinning semantics — if we pin to model X and Redwood pushes a security micro-patch to that model, will we see unexpected behavior?
[05:22] Marco: Patches are non-breaking; we surface model versions and you control auto-upgrade. We can disable auto-updates for pinned models. If a security patch is critical, we coordinate via the enterprise channel and can force patching with notices.
[05:39] Priya: Note to self — include the upgrade opt-in/opt-out docs link in the follow-up.
[05:46] Alex: For rollback testing, can we simulate a faulty model and validate fallback logic?
[05:52] Marco: Yes — we can set up a canary that returns injected errors or degraded responses and then run the rollback trigger; we recommend doing this in a non-prod pilot environment to measure warm-up effects.
[06:08] Tom: Also want an A/B like test for quality — keep 10% on high-quality model, 90% on quantized, monitor golden set metrics.
[06:18] Lena: Sounds good. We'll propose an initial traffic split: 5-10% canary, 30% ramp, and then evaluate. We'll also log model-assigned scores to trace quality regressions.
[06:31] Alex: Small nit — tokenizer mismatch you mentioned earlier, can you add the exact tokenizer version in the config? We hit a token-level difference that altered length predictions.
[06:41] Marco: Yes, tokenizer version and offsets will be in the config blob. It's called out as tokenizer_v2 vs tokenizer_v1 in the catalog; sometimes transcripts autocorrect to token-izer which is fun.
[06:54] Samira: Security follow-up — we need SOC2 evidence and penetration test schedule. Who sends that?
[07:00] Priya: I'll attach our SOC2 pack and latest pen test summary to the follow-up. Expect docs in the repo link.
[07:09] Tom: Anything unresolved on quality? The golden set failed 3/200 examples after switching to q4_8. Are those severe?
[07:20] Marco: They were edgecases — long prompt concatenations with nested tables. For those, we recommend pinning that route to the fp16 (non-quant) variant. We'll flag them in the benchmark CSV.
[07:34] Alex: Good. About cost — can we simulate unit economics with your Optimize tool?
[07:40] Lena: Yes Redwood Optimize can run scenarios — we'll propose 3 profiles: quality-first, balanced, and cost-first with per-token cost estimations and expected latency. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[07:54] Tom: Any legal/procurement blockers? We're still good on standard terms, but we need subprocessor info for healthcare.
[08:01] Lena: We'll include subprocessor list and DPA addendum. Procurement timeline is still on your side.
[08:10] Alex: Ok last thing — scheduling: We want the rollback test week of 11/24, and the Dedicated sizing decision week of 11/29.
[08:19] Lena: Noted. We'll aim to deliver benchmarks and configs by 11/19 so you can review before 11/22.
[08:27] Priya: I'll summarize next steps.
[08:30] Priya: Recap: Marco shares raw bench + config by 11/19; Lena sends pricing + Dedicated template by 11/20; Alex provides extra prompts by 11/22; schedule rollback test for week of 11/24; Samira confirms KMS/peering by 11/21.
[08:48] Alex: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:51] Lena: Thanks, we'll follow up with links and the action item list. Bye.

Resources referenced: security pack link (internal), benchmark CSV (will be shared), model catalog snapshot (rwd-catalog-2026-11-15), pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-2026-11).

End of transcript.
